'''William Lee Steffen''' (25 June 1947 – 29 January 2023)<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=14 November 2018 |title=Expert Report |url=https://www.ipcn.nsw.gov.au/resources/pac/media/files/pac/projects/2018/10/bylong-coal-project/presentations-and-comments/181114-report-of-william-steffen.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320044742/https://www.ipcn.nsw.gov.au/resources/pac/media/files/pac/projects/2018/10/bylong-coal-project/presentations-and-comments/181114-report-of-william-steffen.pdf |archive-date=20 March 2022 |access-date=31 January 2023 |website=NSW Independent Planning Commission}}</ref> was an American-born Australian [[chemist]]. He was the executive director of the [[Australian National University]] (ANU) Climate Change Institute and a member of the Australian [[Climate Commission]] until its dissolution in September 2013.<ref>{{cite web| author=Arup, Tom |url=https://www.theage.com.au/politics/federal/abbott-shuts-down-climate-commission-20130919-2u185.html | title=Abbott shuts down Climate Commission | publisher=The Age | date=19 September 2013 | access-date=24 September 2013}}</ref> From 1998 to 2004, he was the executive director of the [[International Geosphere-Biosphere Programme]], a coordinating body of national environmental change organisations based in [[Stockholm]].<ref name=ANU>[http://www.anu.edu.au/climatechange/content/author/will Professor Will Steffen] ANU Climate Change Institute. Retrieved 11 July 2011.</ref> Steffen was one of the founding climate councillors of the [[Climate Council]], with whom he frequently co-authored reports, and spoke in the media on issues relating to climate change and renewable energy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.climatecouncil.org.au/author/will-steffen/ | title=Will Steffen, Author}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Will Steffen was born in [[Norfolk, Nebraska|Norfolk]], [[Nebraska]], on 25 June 1947.<ref name=":1" /> Steffen completed a BSc in industrial chemistry from the [[University of Missouri]] in 1970. The [[University of Florida]] awarded him an MSc in education in 1972 and a PhD  in chemistry in 1975.<ref name=Council>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20120327174448/http://www.climatescience.org.au/staff/personal/wsteffen.html Professor Will Steffen]}} Australian Research Council.</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rockström |first=Johan |last2=Richardson |first2=Katherine |date=2023-04-21 |title=William Steffen (1947–2023) |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adh9882 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=380 |issue=6642 |pages=245–245 |doi=10.1126/science.adh9882 |issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free }}</ref> He is widely published on [[climate science]]. His research interests ranged over [[climate change]] and [[Earth system science]], with a focus on [[sustainability]]. He wrote on adapting [[land use]] to climate change, bringing human processes into the modelling and analysis of the Earth system, and the history of and future prospects for the relationship between the natural world and humans.<ref name=ANU /> Steffen was also prominent advocating along with [[Paul Crutzen]] the concept of the [[Anthropocene]],<ref>Steffen W, Crutzen PJ and J. R. McNeill JR (2007) [http://www.profwork.org/wsy/earth/Ambio2007.pdf "The Anthropocene: are humans now overwhelming the great forces of Nature?"] ''[[Ambio]]'', '''36''':614–621.</ref> and initiating along with [[Johan Rockström]] an international debate on [[planetary boundaries]] and the "safe operating space" for humanity and in 2018 on the possibility of uncontrolled climate evolution, which stirred considerable scientific debate (Hothouse Earth).<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Rockström | first1 = J. | last2 = Steffen | first2 = W. | last3 = Noone | first3 = K. | last4 = Persson | first4 = Å. | last5 = Chapin Fs | first5 = F. S. | last6 = Lambin | first6 = E. F. | last7 = Lenton | first7 = T. M. | last8 = Scheffer | first8 = M. | last9 = Folke | first9 = C. | last10 = Schellnhuber | doi = 10.1038/461472a | first10 = H. J. | last11 = Nykvist | first11 = B. R. | last12 = De Wit | first12 = C. A. | last13 = Hughes | first13 = T. | last14 = Van Der Leeuw | first14 = S. | last15 = Rodhe | first15 = H. | last16 = Sörlin | first16 = S. | last17 = Snyder | first17 = P. K. | last18 = Costanza | first18 = R. | last19 = Svedin | first19 = U. | last20 = Falkenmark | first20 = M. | last21 = Karlberg | first21 = L. | last22 = Corell | first22 = R. W. | last23 = Fabry | first23 = V. J. | last24 = Hansen | first24 = J. | last25 = Walker | first25 = B. | last26 = Liverman | first26 = D. | last27 = Richardson | first27 = K. | last28 = Crutzen | first28 = P. | last29 = Foley | first29 = J. A. | title = A safe operating space for humanity | journal = Nature | volume = 461 | issue = 7263 | pages = 472–475 | year = 2009 | pmid =  19779433| bibcode = 2009Natur.461..472R | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rockström |first=Johan |last2=Richardson |first2=Katherine |date=2023-04-21 |title=William Steffen (1947–2023) |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.adh9882 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=380 |issue=6642 |pages=245–245 |doi=10.1126/science.adh9882 |issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free }}</ref>

Steffen served as science adviser to the Australian [[Department of Climate Change and Energy Efficiency]].<ref name=ANU /> He was a member of the advisory board of the [[Australian Bureau of Meteorology]] and worked with the Prime Minister's Science, Engineering and Innovation Council. He was also on an advisory panel in Colorado with the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]].<ref name=Council />

Steffen was on the Science Advisory Committee of the APEC Climate Centre in Korea. He was honorary professor at the [[Copenhagen University]]'s Department of Geography and Geology and visiting researcher at the [[Stockholm Resilience Centre]].<ref name=Council /> He was the chair of the Federal Government's Antarctic Science Advisory Committee, and advised the Australian Government in further roles as scientific adviser to the [[Department of Climate Change and Energy Efficiency]] and as expert adviser to the Multi-Party Climate Change Committee.<ref name=Council /> Steffen also sat on the Australian Climate Commission.<ref name="About the Commission">{{cite web| title=About the Commission| url=http://climatecommission.gov.au/about/| publisher=[[Climate Commission]]| access-date=24 September 2013| year=2013}}</ref>

In 2011, he was the principal author of a government climate report, ''The Critical Decade'',<ref name="climatecouncil">{{cite book| author=Climate Commission Secretariat | year=2013 | url=http://www.climatecouncil.org.au/uploads/b7e53b20a7d6573e1ab269d36bb9b07c.pdf | title=The Critical Decade: Climate science, risks and responses| publisher=Department of Climate Change and Energy Efficiency | format=PDF-4.56 Mb | isbn=978-1-921299-50-6| access-date=6 April 2015}}</ref> which advocated that a tax should be placed on carbon.<ref>{{cite news |title=We're bit players in a global drama |date=24 May 2011 |work=[[The Australian]] |url-access=subscription |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/nation/politics/were-bit-players-in-a-global-drama/news-story/23255b5794c5603b42187ea930bcf46c}}</ref><ref>"[http://sj.farmonline.com.au/news/nationalrural/agribusiness-and-general/political/looking-at-the-critical-climate-decade/2174652.aspx Looking at the critical climate decade] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120315001553/http://sj.farmonline.com.au/news/nationalrural/agribusiness-and-general/political/looking-at-the-critical-climate-decade/2174652.aspx |date=15 March 2012 }}". ''Stock Journal'', 27 May 2011.</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=CSIRO scientists cited on climate doomsday |date=5 July 2011 |work=[[The Australian]] |url-access=subscription |url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/nation/politics/csiro-scientists-cited-on-climate-doomsday/news-story/9462897fdf7675191f3669c17c07ce7e}}</ref>

The Australian [[Climate Commission]] was dissolved in 2013. Steffen reflected, "I think we were the first definitive action of the [[Abbott ministry|Abbott government]]. They got rid of us and you could probably measure it in hours rather than days."<ref>{{cite web |last=Wilkinson |first=Marian |date=28 August 2020 |title='You bastards sacked me.' When the climate sceptics arrived |url=https://www.smh.com.au/national/you-bastards-sacked-me-when-the-climate-sceptics-arrived-20200626-p556nn.html |publisher=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> Steffen, along with other dismissed commissioners such as professor [[Tim Flannery]], professor [[Lesley Ann Hughes]], and CEO [[Amanda McKenzie]], launched a new independent organisation — the [[Climate Council]] — in Australia's largest crowdfunding, raising over $1 million in one week.<ref>{{cite web| title=Climate Council nets $1m in donations| url=https://www.sbs.com.au/news/climate-council-nets-1m-in-donations_1| publisher=SBS}}</ref> Steffen remained a climate councillor with the Climate Council.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.climatecouncil.org.au/author/will-steffen/ | title=Will Steffen, Author}}</ref>

In 2018, he was an author of the [[Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C]] published by the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|IPCC]].<ref>IPCC 2018: [https://www.ipcc.ch/sr15/#home-chapter-1 ''Chapter 1: Framing and Context'']. [[Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5 °C]].</ref>

Steffen died from [[pancreatic cancer]] in [[Canberra]] on 29 January 2023, at age 75.<ref>{{cite news |first=Dan |last=Jervis-Bardy |newspaper=Canberra Times |date=31 January 2023 |title=Climate scientist Will Steffen's death prompts outpouring of tributes |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/8066981/brave-climate-warrior-renowned-scientist-will-steffen-dies/?cs=14329 |access-date=31 January 2023 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Readfearn |first=Graham |date=31 January 2023 |title=Will Steffen, 'courageous' climate scientist, dies in Canberra aged 75 |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2023/jan/31/will-steffen-courageous-climate-scientist-dies-in-canberra-aged-75 |access-date=31 January 2023}}</ref> He was married to Carrie for 51 years, and they had a daughter named Sonja.<ref name=":0" />
